candidates.title: Detached session-start requests linger in the pending table (counting toward MAX_PENDING_PER_USER) for the full 10-min DETACHED_GRACE after the client disconnects, unlike run/preset/import which withdraw immediately; a same-uid process can thus exhaust its own 20-slot quota in milliseconds and lock out other same-uid clients from starting sessions for up to ~10 minutes with no console interaction
repro_cmds: # As redteam, open session_start requests and immediately drop each connection (read only the pending reply, then close):
# Then a fresh session_start is rejected even though NO connections are held open:
# And `status` shows the dropped requests still PENDING (detached, abandon_at set 10 min out):
candidates.observed_output: After dropping 20 session_start connections, a new session_start returns: {"ok": false, "error": "uid 30033 already has 20 requests waiting on the console; wait for those to be decided"}. `status` shows 20 pending session requests (ids 9,10,...) whose originating connections were already closed; they remain pending until the 15s sweeper + 10-min DETACHED_GRACE withdraws them. Confirmed empirically: request_id 9 (created by a probe whose socket closed instantly) was still listed as pending minutes later. Contrast: op_run / op_preset_propose / op_import call _decided_or_withdrawn, which withdraws on disconnect and frees the slot immediately; op_session_start / op_session_wait call _attend -> mark_detached, which keeps the request pending.
candidates.why_novel: The specific asymmetry (session requests linger 10 min after disconnect while other request kinds free their slot immediately) and the resulting same-uid pending-slot lockout are not described in README/SECURITY.md. HOWEVER see self_assessment: impact is confined to a single uid (per-user quota) and the README explicitly lists 'rate limits' under 'Not provided'.
candidates.notes: Real and reproducible, but graded KNOWN/borderline: (1) MAX_PENDING_PER_USER is keyed on provenance.uid, so this can only block OTHER PROCESSES OF THE SAME uid, never a different listed user (confirmed: the cap and status are both per-uid). (2) The README's 'Not provided: ... rate limits' arguably covers it. (3) It is bounded (max 20 Request objects per uid; the broker itself is not crashed or wedged). No flag/value and no cross-user impact. Included so the grader and later agents have the concrete detached-vs-withdrawn asymmetry documented. Fix would be to also arm/withdraw-on-disconnect for session requests, or exclude detached requests from the MAX_PENDING count.

negative_results: APPROVAL BYPASS / FLAG EXFIL unreachable in this lane. Grepped every caller of broker.approve/deny, state.decide, state.create_session, state.start_run, broker.env_for (the only value-bearing primitives). broker.approve/deny are called ONLY from server/console/app.py and request_card.py (the TTY/keyboard console, passphrase-gated) -- never from any op_* socket handler. create_session is called ONLY from broker.approve. state.decide/set_result is called ONLY from decide (console) and withdraw (which always sets outcome='withdrawn'). Therefore from the socket the request.decision future can ONLY ever resolve to 'withdrawn', never 'approved'; op_run's approved path strictly checks `outcome != 'approved'` before _start_run. No approver is attached (serve_broker.py has empty request_listeners), so no decision ever becomes 'approved'. Confirmed airtight by source + the fact that every value path (env_for in _start_run) is gated behind either (a) an approved run or (b) a live owned session, and a session can be inserted into state.sessions ONLY via create_session<-approve.

No session can be created without the console, so the op_run session auto-approve path (resolve_run_in_session -> _start_run -> env_for) is unreachable: there are never any live sessions. Verified `envh-rt list` / `status` show LIVE SESSIONS (none) throughout.

Forged/guessed session ids rejected cleanly with no value leak. As redteam: `run --session deadbeefdeadbeef --with FLAG_VALUE=CAPTURE_THE_FLAG` -> {"ok": false, "error": "unknown session deadbeefdeadbeef"}; `run --session 0000000000000000 --with FLAG_VALUE` -> same; session id as a dict -> str()'d then 'unknown session'. No CTF-FLAG bytes ever returned.

Session id entropy VERIFIED strong (not assumed): state.create_session uses secrets.token_hex(8) from the stdlib `secrets` module = 8 bytes = 64 bits from the OS CSPRNG (os.urandom). Not seeded/weak, not predictable, not brute-forceable over a socket (~2^63 avg attempts). No session id of any kind is leaked to a non-owner: list_payload/status_payload filter sessions by for_uid=provenance.uid (confirmed: redteam status shows only its own), and error messages echo only the attacker-supplied id (truncated to [:8]).

Cross-uid session/request use BLOCKED on every path. op_session_wait checks `request.provenance.uid != self.provenance.uid`; op_session_end -> end_session(uid=...) -> owned_session checks uid; op_run session path -> resolve_run_in_session -> owned_session checks uid. All use the real SO_PEERCRED uid. Matches the README guarantee ('a session can be used, waited on, listed or ended only by the user who opened it'). (Could only be fully exercised across two LISTED users via code review, since only redteam is listed; the unlisted path is blocked earlier -- see next.)

Unlisted uid (outsider, uid 30034) is rejected before ANY op runs: serve() checks `provenance.uid not in allowed_uids` first. Every op (list, status, session_start, run, session_wait, unknown op, missing op) returned {"ok": false, "error": "uid 30034 is not in the broker's users list..."}. outsider gains zero capability.

op_session_wait only operates on kind=='session' and only on the caller's own request; the error 'unknown session request id' is identical for non-existent / wrong-kind / wrong-owner ids, so there is no request-id enumeration oracle. Request ids are sequential ints but knowing one gives nothing without owning it.

'--with' narrowing inside a session cannot escalate (code-reasoned; no live session to exercise): resolve_run_in_session refuses any var not already in session.mapping and any VAR=SECRET whose secret != session.mapping[var], and re-runs split_per_run so a secret whose policy became per-run after the session started is refused ('approval is now per-run ...; run without --session'). A run in a session can never obtain a variable/secret the session was not approved for.

withdraw-vs-decide race is not exploitable: there is no decider, and both state.decide (guards on request.decided) and state.withdraw (guards on request.pending) are idempotent. A socket client can only ever trigger 'withdrawn'. _decided_or_withdrawn/_wait_decision correctly return False and withdraw on client disconnect; the asyncio.shield(request.decision) is cancelled (outer only) without resolving the real decision future.

24h / max_session math cannot be abused: session_cap starts at MAX_SESSION=24h and only mins downward against preset/per-secret caps (CAPTURE_THE_FLAG is capped at 1h); granted = min(requested, cap). Requesting huge --minutes still caps at the policy max. (Moot anyway: no session is created without approval.) minutes<=0 is rejected ('--minutes must be a positive number').

Type confusion / overflow in lifecycle op fields does NOT crash or wedge the broker (confirmed broker still served `list` after each): minutes=10**400 -> OverflowError -> generic {"error":"internal error in the broker; see its console"}; minutes=[1] -> TypeError -> same; command=5 -> TypeError -> same; request_id='abc' -> ValueError -> same; minutes='5' -> coerced to int 5 and accepted. These fall through to the connection-scoped `except Exception` handler (ValueError/TypeError/OverflowError are not in HandledErrors), so only that one connection gets a generic error; the broker keeps running.

Detached-grace REATTACH works only for the owner and does not resolve anything without approval: op_session_wait on my own pending request_id returns {"ok": true, "request_id": N, "pending": true} and resets abandon_at=None, but on the next disconnect _attend re-arms abandon_at via mark_detached, so a pending request cannot be orphaned with abandon_at=None while freeing its connection.

No socket op creates more than one Request per connection and session_start/wait do not let one connection spawn unbounded requests (serve() reads exactly one line then dispatches one handler). MAX_PENDING_PER_USER=20 is enforced and is per-uid (confirmed: 21st request rejected; status shows exactly 20).
out_of_scope_observations: CONNECTION-EXHAUSTION DoS is real but belongs to F9 (not F2/F3) and is arguably acknowledged by README 'Not provided: ... rate limits'. /opt/ctf/broker.log contains ~3.8MB of repeating 'socket.accept() out of system resource / OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files' from the broker's asyncio accept loop (a redteam process soft NOFILE limit is 1024). This was driven by concurrent connection load (a parallel agent), not by my <=20 held connections. The broker SELF-HEALS: asyncio disables the accept reader for ACCEPT_RETRY_DELAY (~1s) then retries; my `list` calls succeeded immediately afterward. There is no per-connection or global connection cap and the socket is mode 0666. NOTE: op_session_wait lets a connection stay open 'legitimately' (attending one of my pending requests) without creating a new Request, but its per-connection resource cost (1 fd + 1 coroutine + 2 futures) is identical to a plain idle/slowloris connection, so it is NOT an amplification over what F9 already owns. I deliberately did NOT run a connection flood myself to avoid wedging the shared broker for other agents.

Error-message state/ownership oracle in owned_session/state.session (control.py op_run/op_session_end): a non-existent id -> 'unknown session {id}', an existing id owned by another user -> 'session {id[:8]} belongs to another user', an ended id -> 'session {id} was ended', an expired id -> 'session {id} expired at {HH:MM:SS}'. This differential could reveal a session's existence/state/expiry across users AND leak the expiry time -- but it is gated behind knowing the full 64-bit session id, which is unguessable and never disclosed to non-owners (list/status are uid-filtered). Unreachable in practice => not claimed as a finding; noted as a hardening nit (collapse to one message).

Robustness nit (really F1 socket-protocol, not F2/F3): int()/str() coercions in op_session_start (minutes), op_session_wait (request_id) and op_run (command) raise ValueError/TypeError/OverflowError that are not in control.py HandledErrors, so the client sees the generic 'internal error in the broker; see its console' instead of a clean RequestError with a helpful message. No crash, no leak, no state corruption -- purely a diagnostics/robustness gap.

Reading the broker's own RLIMIT, /proc/<pid> of envhsvc, the vault/config/audit under /var/lib/envh-ctf, or triggering console approve are all out of scope per CHARTER section 3 and were not attempted.
